mainEntity.name: How does a room addition compare to a garage conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Converting an attached garage is typically faster and uses the existing walls and roof, whereas building a ground-up addition offers complete freedom in placement, layout, and ceiling heights. A garage conversion avoids pouring a completely detached foundation, but it requires raising concrete floors, adding insulation, updating electrical, and sacrificing vehicle parking and storage. A new ground-up room addition preserves garage functionality and keeps your primary layout intact, but it demands new foundation excavation, framing from scratch, and full exterior roof integration.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion utilizes an existing structure and roof but sacrifices parking, while a ground-up addition preserves vehicle storage but requires a new foundation.
